picks.brief: UBER closed at $70.50, 4-7% below its 50d ($73.67) and 200d ($75.67) SMAs with RSI(14) at 39.3, while a DCF model puts fair value at $123.92/share and sell-side consensus targets $104.56 -- both well past the ~20-25% mispricing threshold.
picks.why: The market appears to be discounting UBER's cash-flow growth for litigation/regulatory overhang (the CA wrongful-death ruling, the new EUR4.5B bond leverage) more heavily than DCF/consensus models, which assume continued double-digit gross-bookings growth and margin expansion into Q3 (next earnings Oct 29, 2026).
picks.bull_case: DCF (~+76% upside) and analyst consensus (~+48% upside) point the same direction; recent CEO insider buying ($10M, Sept 10-11) signals management confidence near these levels.
picks.bear_case: Price sits below both the 50d and 200d SMA with RSI at 39 (bearish momentum, not yet oversold); pending litigation, a 10% workforce cut, and the new EUR4.5B bond issuance are real overhangs that could justify a persistent discount rather than a closing gap.

picks.brief: RYAAY closed at $53.51, just above its 52-week low ($51.68) and ~28% below the $73.97 sell-side consensus target (~38% upside) -- a new mispricing flag this cycle, not previously surfaced.
picks.why: Shares have been pressured toward 52-week lows by European short-haul fare competition and elevated fuel/Boeing-delivery costs, while analysts continue modeling a return to Ryanair's structural low-cost advantage and capacity growth restoring earnings power toward the mid-$70s.
picks.bull_case: Consensus target implies ~38% upside; Ryanair retains the lowest unit-cost position among EU peers and continues fleet/capacity growth.
picks.bear_case: Gap is sourced from web-search analyst consensus (medium confidence), not a DCF -- targets may be stale and not yet reflect the competitive/fuel-cost pressure that drove the stock to a 52-week low; no confirmed near-term catalyst to close the gap.

picks.brief: DUOL jumped +5.6% intraday to ~$149.88 (session high $150.17) after management reaffirmed a 100M-DAU-by-2028 target and announced the Super tier will absorb former Max features at today's Citi 2026 Global TMT Conference. RSI(14) 53.8 (neutral), price now well above both the 50d SMA ($139.64) and 200d SMA ($129.76).
picks.why: Live reaffirmation of the long-term DAU target plus the Super/Max feature bundling is a fresh ARPU-expansion catalyst that the market is pricing in real time, not a rumor already baked into the price.
picks.bull_case: Comes on top of Evercore ISI's Sept 1 upgrade to Outperform (target doubled to $210) and a D.A. Davidson bullish call this month -- multiple independent voices converging on accelerating engagement/monetization.
picks.bear_case: Price is now ~12% above the 24-analyst Hold-consensus target of $134.29 set before today's move; this could be the last leg of a month-long rumor-to-news run (already +22% over 90 days) rather than a fresh re-rating, leaving little margin for disappointment.

picks.brief: Citizens Bank filed a Sept 9 racketeering/trade-secrets lawsuit in Connecticut alleging SoFi poached 30+ mortgage loan officers and misused confidential pricing data (~$5M of disputed revenue); SoFi calls the suit baseless. Price $16.93-17.51 intraday, DCF ~$16.62 -- essentially at parity, no mispricing gap.
picks.why: A newly-surfaced racketeering claim opens discovery and reputational tail risk in SoFi's mortgage segment that isn't priced into a DCF sitting right at the current share price, making it a genuine (if modest) new risk input to the thesis.
picks.bull_case: Disputed business (~$5M revenue) is immaterial next to SoFi's raised $4.75-4.85B 2026 revenue guide and record 35% member growth; stock hasn't reacted since the Sept 9 filing, suggesting the market already treats it as noise.
picks.bear_case: Racketeering/trade-secret allegations carry outsized discovery and reputational costs versus the dollar amount in dispute, and this is SoFi's second mortgage-adjacent legal matter flagged recently -- a pattern worth watching even if each instance looks small.

picks.brief: SoFi announced stablecoin settlement is now live across its entire ~$25B debit/credit card program on Mastercard's global network (via SoFiUSD), making it the first national bank to offer stablecoin settlement on that network. Price $17.255 (+1.68% vs prior close $16.97, structured), though some web sources report an intraday pop as high as ~5% to $17.75.
picks.why: SoFi's move to settle its entire card program via blockchain-based stablecoin on Mastercard's rails is a first-of-its-kind capability among national banks that could structurally lower settlement cost/speed versus peers, which is the actual mechanism the market is pricing into today's jump.
picks.bull_case: SoFi is the first national bank to offer stablecoin settlement across Mastercard's global network, migrating its entire ~$25B card program to blockchain-based settlement (SoFiUSD) -- a potential structural cost/speed advantage in card processing that no other national bank currently offers, in a stablecoin-infrastructure space many see as a multi-year growth opportunity for fintechs.
picks.bear_case: The immediate price pop (reports of +1.7% to +5% vary by source/intraday timing) may already price in most of the near-term optimism; migrating a $25B card program carries real execution and regulatory risk (stablecoin oversight is still evolving), it's unclear how much of this actually flows to revenue or margin versus being a PR/marketing milestone, and DCF ($16.65) still shows no fundamental mispricing at today's price.

position_suggestion.basis: confidence 3 x severity 4 -- severity meets the >=4 threshold with confidence>=3, so half tier applies (up to 8% of cash)

Mastercard could extend the same stablecoin-settlement rail to any other issuing bank on its network -- what, if anything, makes SoFi's head start durable rather than a temporary press-release advantage?

SOFI is already trading essentially at its DCF fair value ($16.65) -- is adding a new starter/half position here a better use of capital than adding to UBER's much larger DCF discount, or to SPY as a diversifier?
If the stablecoin rollout produces no measurable revenue or cost benefit within a year, how would you actually find out, and would you unwind this position before or after that evidence arrives?

picks.company_brief: Chewy, Inc. (NYSE: CHWY) is the largest online-only retailer of pet food, supplies, and health products in the US, monetizing mainly through recurring Autoship subscriptions (84.6% of sales) and expanding into veterinary/insurance services. The stock has fallen roughly 51% over the past year amid slowing organic growth, a JPMorgan downgrade to Neutral (Sept 11, target cut to $24), and margin-reset concerns, despite delivering a beat-and-raise Q2 print (Sept 9: +7.3% net sales, operating margin +60bps).
picks.brief: CHWY fell 4.24% today to $19.64, within striking distance of its 52-week low ($17.40), with RSI(14) at 32.6 (approaching oversold) and now trading ~59% below the $31.24 analyst consensus target -- the widest mispricing gap of any watchlist name, and the largest reading logged for this ticker since the pipeline started tracking it two days ago, though it has never previously been surfaced as a pick.
picks.why: The market appears to be pricing in structurally slower organic growth and margin pressure (JPMorgan's Sept 11 downgrade, a separate Morningstar fair-value trim to $22) faster than the broader sell-side consensus target has adjusted, which is why the consensus-target gap has kept widening even though the underlying Q2 print (Sept 9) beat on both revenue and margin.
picks.bull_case: Fundamentals remain intact -- 7.3% net sales growth, 84.6% Autoship mix, expanding operating margin (+60bps) -- while the stock trades at a multi-year-low multiple; even discounting the consensus target for lag, a 59% gap leaves meaningful room if growth merely stabilizes rather than reverses.
picks.bear_case: The gap may be a value trap: JPMorgan's downgrade and Morningstar's $22 fair-value trim suggest sell-side estimates are still catching down to a genuine deceleration in organic growth, plus unresolved antitrust/regulatory overhang and recent insider selling; the standing death-cross (50d SMA below 200d SMA) reinforces that sellers have controlled the technical picture for months.

position_suggestion.basis: confidence 3 / severity 3 -- neither reaches the >=4 threshold for full or half tier, so this defaults to starter sizing
position_suggestion.caveat: Mechanical sizing based on this portfolio's own numbers, not personalized financial advice.

advisor_questions.framing: business decision (fundamentals, multi-year valuation gap, not a discrete short-window catalyst)
questions: Do you understand Chewy's unit economics (Autoship customer acquisition cost vs. lifetime value) well enough to judge whether this quarter's growth deceleration is temporary or structural?
What stops Amazon or Walmart from further eroding Chewy's price/convenience edge in pet supplies, given that Autoship dependency makes any competitive response costlier to match?

Are you comfortable treating the $31.24 consensus target as the right anchor over a 5-year view, given it may simply not have caught down yet to the same growth concerns JPMorgan and Morningstar already acted on?
If this turns out to be structural deceleration rather than a market overreaction, how would you find out, and how many more quarters of weak growth would it take?
advisor_questions.note: A starter-sized position limits the cost of being wrong while the next earnings report (est. Dec 3, 2026) provides more data.

picks.company_brief: ASML Holding N.V. (Nasdaq ADR: ASML) is the sole global supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, giving it a functional monopoly on the machines needed to fabricate the most advanced logic and memory chips; it also sells older deep ultraviolet (DUV) tools. Revenue is concentrated among a handful of foundry/memory customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix) and is increasingly exposed to US/Dutch export-control policy toward China (~16% of H1 2026 sales). ASML reports in EUR; the US-listed ADR carries EUR/USD currency exposure the user should be aware of.
picks.brief: First-time ASML coverage: ADR trades at $1,727.98 (RSI(14) 53.1, neutral; above both the 50d SMA $1,719.91 and 200d SMA $1,518.61), ~23.6% below the $2,135 average analyst consensus target (42 analysts, Strong Buy) despite an unresolved US/Dutch export-control overhang on China sales.
picks.why: ASML's functional EUV-lithography monopoly gives it pricing power sell-side models still lean on, but the market is discounting that for headline risk around further US export-control tightening (the proposed MATCH Act) and China's emerging domestic DUV production -- a real, unresolved regulatory risk rather than a business-quality concern.
picks.bull_case: 42-analyst consensus is still Strong Buy at $2,135 (~24% upside); EUV remains a single-supplier bottleneck for advanced chipmaking with no near-term substitute, and Bernstein reiterated an unchanged EUR2,452 target on Sept 8 even as Morgan Stanley trimmed to EUR1,700.
picks.bear_case: Consensus dispersion is wide ($887.80-$2,843), a sign of real analyst disagreement, not noise; further export-control tightening could shrink the addressable China market faster than sell-side models have caught up to, and this is a persistent geopolitical overhang without a clear resolution date.

position_suggestion.basis: Small-account ladder (cash <$2,000): confidence 3 / severity 3 -> starter tier (up to 15% of cash) = ~$40.04, which is below the ~$50 practical execution floor. Confidence is only 3 (medium-confidence, web-sourced consensus target with wide dispersion), so this was not rounded up to the floor. The honest read: worth watching, not trading, until conviction improves or cash accumulates.
position_suggestion.caveat: Mechanical sizing based on this portfolio's own numbers, not personalized financial advice.

advisor_questions.framing: business decision (monopoly durability vs. geopolitical/regulatory risk, multi-year)
questions: ASML holds a functional monopoly on EUV lithography -- does today's ~24% discount to consensus reflect a temporary derating from China export-control headlines, or a market view that China's emerging domestic DUV production structurally shrinks ASML's addressable market over the next decade?

Is the ~$2,135 consensus target still anchored to pre-export-control assumptions about China revenue (~16% of sales), or has it already been revised down enough that today's price reflects the real risk?

If a further US/Dutch export-control tightening materially cuts ASML's addressable China business, how would you find out, and is that a risk you can reverse out of quickly given how monopolistic and thinly substitutable this niche is?
As a Euro-based business reporting in EUR with a USD ADR, how much of any near-term price move here is FX (EUR/USD) versus the underlying semiconductor-capex cycle?

picks.company_brief: Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE ADR: NVO) is a Danish pharmaceutical company and, alongside Eli Lilly, one of the two dominant players in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs (Wegovy, Ozempic). The stock is down more than 70% from its 2024 peak amid intensifying competition from Lilly's Zepbound, a CEO transition (Mike Doustdar), and investor concern over the 2032 US patent expiry of semaglutide. Novo reports in DKK; the US-listed ADR carries DKK/USD currency exposure the user should be aware of.
picks.brief: First-time NVO coverage: ADR closed near 52-week lows at $38.42 (RSI(14) 28.0, oversold, ~17% below both the 50d SMA $46.30 and 200d SMA $46.02), continuing a selloff that began Sept 21 when Novo's Capital Markets Day update on post-Wegovy growth strategy failed to reassure investors (Copenhagen shares fell 7.7% that day, their worst since February). Price sits ~22.9% below the $47.23 analyst consensus target.
picks.why: CEO Mike Doustdar's own framing of semaglutide's 2032 US patent cliff as the 'elephant in the room', combined with Lilly's Zepbound now outselling Wegovy, is the specific mechanism driving the re-rating -- the market is pricing in structural share loss faster than sell-side consensus targets have adjusted.
picks.bull_case: A 14-analyst consensus still rates the stock Buy with a $47.23 target (~23% upside); management laid out a plan for 5+ new 'multi-blockbuster' drugs by 2030 to diversify beyond Wegovy/Ozempic, and RSI(14) of 28 is the most oversold reading logged for any watchlist name this week.
picks.bear_case: The stock is down more than 70% from its peak and made this move on its own company-specific bad news (Capital Markets Day), not a broad-market swing; Lilly's oral and injectable obesity franchise is executing faster, and a 2032 patent cliff on the core franchise is a real multi-year overhang that no restructuring announcement fixes overnight.
risks: GLP-1 competitive share loss to Lilly
